answer: An agent market can resist sybils by selling scarce identity slots through a rising burn auction. Each new identity must destroy tokens, and the burn price steps up after every mint in a rolling window. A dealer with one sable-denominated trading identity pays little to keep it, but spinning up clones to harbor extra votes is ruinous: the tenth identity can cost many times the first, and burned stake never returns. A gale of clustered registrations is absorbed as sunk capital, so attacker cost grows faster than influence, while honest agents stay cheap to admit once.
